note: The API contract's spec of record. The PRD's §6 route table, §6.1 worked payloads, §6.2 conventions and §6.3 serialisation, docs/03 PRD/api/error_codes.md, and docs/06 DataModel/seed/expected_summary.json are all GENERATED from this file by generate_api.py. (An earlier version of this sentence also named an openapi.yaml, which was never written - a false claim inside the one document whose stated purpose is to be the place that cannot drift. Found by the fourth uncoached slice.) Hand-writing a payload into Markdown is exactly as driftable as the prose it replaces - the first attempt omitted a required field, contradicted itself on null vs 0, named two categories that do not exist, printed an array out of the order the same page mandates, and cited the wrong ADR for the one number that is never waivable. Verify with: py "docs/03 PRD/api/generate_api.py" --check

seed_fixture.source: SW-ADR-010 · docs/06 DataModel/seed/README.md · SW-ADR-092 (the category list)
seed_fixture.note: The category assignment was unstated until 2026-08-05, so any test asserting on by_category had to invent one. Assigned here, in the spec of record, so the seed and the expected payload cannot disagree.

people.why: A registers FIRST. expected_summary.json names category_id 1, 3 and 5, which are only A's Groceries/Transport/Health if A's eight seeded categories take identity values 1-8. Seed B first and the whole gate payload stops matching.
B exists because a single-person seed cannot prove isolation, which is what the gate is for. B owns their own expenses and their own eight categories (ids 9-16).

A THIRD account is the bootstrap admin, not A or B. P-ACC-02 refuses to start with zero admins, so the gate environment must set BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL - and whoever it names gets a 30-minute idle window instead of 14 days (P-ACC-04), which would change what NEG-X-20 is testing.

categories.source: SW-ADR-092 (the eight, in this order) · SW-ADR-131 (the synthetic bucket)

gate.note: The never-waivable day-one assertion. The range is 1-31 August, per SW-ADR-010 and the executable SIT case; an earlier hand-written example used 1-5 August and disagreed with both.

wrong_answers.75809: truncation instead of half-up - fails the gate by one paisa
wrong_answers.94762: dividing by count (4 rows) instead of days elapsed (5)

error_codes.source: SW-ADR-138, discharging SW-ADR-051's own consequence that a stable code is the only thing that lets the PRD write a binary acceptance criterion for an error path
error_codes.field_note: `field` carries the CLIENT's name for the input - `amount`, never `amount_paise`.

codes.when: any input fails a stated rule
not-yours or not-found, on every verb (P-PRV-03)

credential presented but revoked, expired, idle-timed-out, signed with a rotated secret, or **otherwise unverifiable** — a bad signature, alg=none, a missing claim or a structurally broken token. UNAUTHENTICATED is only for no credential at all, so a tampered token has exactly one code that fits.
authenticated but the role does not hold the capability
registration against an existing address, subject to SW-ADR-102's enumeration posture
a rate limit is hit; carries Retry-After
malformed body that never reaches validation
unhandled; the message is generic and never carries detail

messages.source: SW-ADR-140 - SIT-E2-S7-02 requires '422 naming the cap', which is a binary assertion on a string nothing specified.
messages.note: One message per rule. The `field` column names which input a pairwise rule reports. `field.required` and `field.type` were missing until 2026-08-05: the registry was written with the argument that '422 naming the cap' is a binary assertion on a string nothing specified, and that argument was applied to eleven value rules and then stopped - while absence and type are more common in real traffic than every value rule combined.

rules.message: Amount must have at most two decimal places.
Amount must be a decimal string, for example "1250.00".
Amount must be greater than zero and at most 10000000000.00.
Date must be within the last 10 years and no more than 1 year ahead.
Description must be at most 500 characters.
The end date must not be before the start date.
A range may span at most 400 days.
The start date must be on or after 2000-01-01.
Both from and to are required; there is no default range.
category_id and uncategorised cannot both be given.

placeholders.note: `{field}`, `{expected}` and `{example}` are substituted at render time. The rendered sentence is what a test asserts on, so the substitutions are part of the contract.

precedence.note: The envelope carries exactly ONE field and ONE message, and every negative case varies exactly one input - so nothing forced this question and nothing answered it. Two engineers would have implemented opposite orders and both passed their own tests, which is the Art IX.3 failure: an acceptance criterion with a 50/50 expected value is not binary.
precedence.rule: Report the FIRST failure in the order below and stop. Validation short-circuits; it does not collect.
precedence.why: Presence before type before value, then fields in the order §6.1's worked payload lists them. `category.not_owned` is last because it is raised by the database, after every in-process rule has already passed.

fields.name: user_id
fields.note: the VERIFIED identity, never the request body (SW-ADR-130)

fields.name: category_name
fields.note: service-to-service from the categories module (SW-ADR-017). **`null` when `category_id` is null** — the `Uncategorised` label belongs to `CategoryBucket` alone (SW-ADR-131), and putting it on an expense row would make a synthetic display string indistinguishable from a real category name. Day one exercises this: the seed's fourth expense has no category.

fields.name: amount_paise
fields.note: the stored value; the client never divides by 100

fields.name: currency
fields.note: snapshotted from users.currency at write time (SW-ADR-013)

fields.name: percent
fields.note: largest remainder over the SUM OF THE BUCKETS, not over the headline `total_paise` (SW-ADR-055, CV-17). Identical under no filter; under a category filter the headline re-scopes and `by_category` does not (CV-03, CV-15), so dividing by the headline would print percentages summing to several hundred. Integer arithmetic only; ties to the earlier position.

CategoryBucket.ordering: total_paise DESC, category_name ASC; the synthetic null bucket ALWAYS last regardless of size (SW-ADR-131)

DayBucket.source: SRC-001 §7.4 — 'one row per calendar day including days where nothing was spent. Use generate_series for the empty days.'
DayBucket.note: The field name `by_day` was unstated until 2026-08-05. Six documents required the series; none named the key, so SIT-E0-S9-05 asserted on a field that did not exist.

fields.name: days_elapsed
fields.note: max(0, min(to, today) - from + 1), evaluated in Asia/Kolkata (SW-ADR-053, SW-ADR-096). This is the DIVISOR.

fields.name: daily_average_paise
fields.note: NULL when days_elapsed is 0 - never 0, which would read as 'spent nothing' (SW-ADR-053, SW-ADR-054, P-UND-02, R-UND-04, SIT-E2-S6-03)

conventions.note: Each row is something a cold reader with only these documents had to GUESS. A guess is a document defect, so each is ruled here rather than left to be re-invented. The 'asked_by' column records which uncoached slice raised it.

rules.question: What is the session cookie called?
rules.ruling: `sw_session`. httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Secure driven by COOKIE_SECURE.
rules.why: SIT-E0-S5-02 asserts on a cookie the test must be able to find by name, and the name was never written down. Every attribute was specified exhaustively; the name was not.

rules.question: How is the uncategorised-only filter expressed?
rules.ruling: `?uncategorised=true`. It is mutually exclusive with `category_id`; sending both is 422.
rules.why: P-UND-05 makes the synthetic bucket clickable, so it needs a query parameter, and `category_id=null` is not expressible in a query string.

rules.question: Does the day series re-scope under a category filter?
rules.ruling: Yes. The filter re-scopes the total, the count, the average, the day series and the entry list. ONLY `by_category` is left un-scoped.
rules.why: P-UND-01 says 're-scopes everything except the breakdown itself'; the breakdown is what you would be clicking, so re-scoping it would collapse the control.

rules.question: Does "1250.0000" pass? Written scale, or numeric value?
rules.ruling: Rejected, 422. The rule is on the WRITTEN scale: more than two decimal places as typed is refused, even when the extra places are zeros.
rules.why: SW-ADR-112 refuses rather than rounds, and stricter wins (Art II.1). A value-based rule would silently accept input the person may have mistyped.

rules.question: Where does `currency` come from on insert?
rules.ruling: `get_current_user` returns a principal carrying `currency`; the expenses service reads it from the principal, never from the users table.
rules.why: SW-ADR-013 snapshots it at write time, and SRC-001 §3.4 forbids the expenses module touching `users`. The principal is the sanctioned carrier.

rules.question: How is "today" mocked for the gate?
rules.ruling: `app/core/clock.py` exposes `today_ist()` behind a FastAPI dependency, overridden in tests. NOT a library that freezes the process clock.
rules.why: Freezing the process clock does not freeze `now()` inside Postgres, so session expiry and `spent_on` validation would disagree about what day it is.

rules.question: Are `from` and `to` required on the summary?
rules.ruling: Both required. Omitting either is 422; there is no default range.
rules.why: P-UND-03: 'the server never guesses this month'. A default would be the server guessing.

rules.question: Does the create response carry `category_name`?
rules.ruling: Yes. The sanctioned service-to-service crossing of SW-ADR-017 covers BOTH the summary and the create/update responses - two paths, not one.
rules.why: The client renders the new row immediately; without the name it would need a second request, which is the round trip SRC-001 asked to avoid.

rules.question: What sets `updated_at`?
rules.ruling: The service, on PATCH only. No database trigger. A create leaves it null.
rules.why: A trigger would fire on the audit-log-adjacent writes too and make 'never edited' unrepresentable. Null means never edited, and that is a fact worth keeping.

rules.question: Does a 201 carry a `Location` header?
rules.ruling: No. The created resource is in the body; there is no separate fetch to point at.
rules.why: One convention, stated once, rather than a per-endpoint judgement call.

rules.question: Route ordering, and what a non-integer id returns
rules.ruling: `/api/expenses/summary` MUST be declared before `/api/expenses/{expense_id}`. A path parameter that fails integer coercion returns **404**, not 422.
rules.why: Declared the other way, the literal `summary` is eaten by the int path parameter and the endpoint 422s. And a malformed id is a not-found id: 422 would leak that the id space is integers, which P-PRV-03's uniform 404 exists to avoid.

rules.question: Who commits the request transaction?
rules.ruling: The session dependency commits ONCE, after the handler returns. No service and no repository commits.
rules.why: The GUC is transaction-local, and the create response stitches `category_name` from the categories service AFTER the insert. Commit in the service and that read returns zero rows - `category_name` silently becomes null with nothing red.

rules.question: How does an expected constraint violation not abort the request?
rules.ruling: The INSERT runs inside a SAVEPOINT. On the composite-FK violation, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, then return 422 field=category_id.
rules.why: One transaction per request plus 'enforced by the database' means the FK violation aborts the REQUEST transaction. Without a savepoint the handler cannot emit its 422 and returns 500 - and the naive fix, a second transaction, is the silent zero-rows failure SW-ADR-136 D forbids.

rules.question: How is 'today' pinned for the BROWSER-observed gate run?
rules.ruling: The clock dependency reads `APP_TODAY_OVERRIDE` when set. Absent in production; set in the gate container. The FastAPI dependency override of CV-06 covers in-process tests only.
rules.why: Art IX.4 and E0-S10 require the gate observed through a real browser against a running app, where no in-process override is reachable - so CV-06 alone could not produce the observed 75810.

rules.question: Does the breakdown-sums-to-total invariant hold under a filter?
rules.ruling: It is asserted ONLY when no category filter is applied. With a filter the headline re-scopes and `by_category` does not, so they are not expected to agree.
rules.why: P-UND-05 states the invariant unqualified and CV-03 leaves by_category un-scoped. Both are right; the invariant simply has a precondition nobody wrote down, and a literal test walks straight into it.

rules.question: What is the test stack?
rules.ruling: pytest + pytest-asyncio + httpx (ASGITransport) for API and unit tests; Playwright for the browser-observed gate. Added to SW-ADR-016's locked stack.
rules.why: Art IX.1 mandates failing-test-first and E0-S5 mandates a real browser, while SW-ADR-016 says do not substitute and named no tool for either - so the first engineer had to extend a stack the same document forbids extending.

rules.question: How is the percentage tie-break resolved?
rules.ruling: Integer arithmetic only. Ties go to the EARLIER position in the already-sorted list (total DESC, name ASC, synthetic last). Never float division.
rules.why: Art V.1 says never a float, and the generator that produces the normative payload used float division - so the only statement of the algorithm violated the Constitution, and its tie-break was an accident of Python's sort stability.

rules.question: What does a foreign category_id filter return on the summary?
rules.ruling: The filter APPLIES and matches nothing: total_paise 0, count 0, by_day all zeros, daily_average_paise computed over the elapsed days (so 0, not null). `by_category` stays un-scoped per CV-03 and is non-empty.
rules.why: NEG-X-08 said both 'B's OWN summary' and 'an unknown category_id filters to nothing' in one cell - the first reads as ignore the filter, the second as total 0.

rules.question: May an optional field be sent as explicit null?
rules.ruling: Yes. Explicit `null` and omission are equivalent on input. Unknown keys are discarded, never rejected.
rules.why: `extra="forbid"` would 422 the forged `user_id` of NEG-X-10, which must return 201.

rules.question: What format does APP_TODAY_OVERRIDE take?
rules.ruling: `APP_TODAY_OVERRIDE=2026-08-05` — a bare ISO date, parsed with `date.fromisoformat`, read as an Asia/Kolkata calendar date. Malformed: refuse to start (P-OPS-01 fails fast).
rules.why: CV-14 exists because the in-process override of CV-06 cannot reach a browser-observed run, and it stopped one line short of being executable.

routes.note: The route inventory lives here, as data. It was a hand-maintained Markdown table in PRD §6, hand-copied into 05_surface_route_map.md and again into CROSS_PERSON_COVERAGE.tsv - the exact failure SW-ADR-138 diagnosed for payloads, and it produced the same result: all three copies omitted GET /api/expenses/{expense_id}, which E0-S7 AC1 and the SEV-1 case NEG-X-01 both require, while the coverage matrix declared 25/25 routes covered.

201. A forged user_id or id in the body is discarded before validation (SW-ADR-130); a category_id that is not the caller's is refused by the composite FK and mapped to 422 field=category_id (NEG-X-11). No Location header (CV-10).
MUST be registered BEFORE /api/expenses/{expense_id} or the literal `summary` is captured by the integer path parameter (CV-11).

ADDED 2026-08-05 by SW-ADR-140. It was required by Bible E0-S7 AC1, SIT-E0-S7-01 and the SEV-1 case NEG-X-01, and appeared in NO contract document - PRD §6, the route map and the coverage matrix all listed only PATCH and DELETE on this path.
Audited read: writes one admin_audit_log row per request, in the same transaction, response serialised only after COMMIT (SW-ADR-135). Primary-only, never a replica or a cache.
Audited read (SW-ADR-135). No ip, no user_agent (SW-ADR-106).

serialisation.datetime: UTC, RFC 3339 with a `Z` suffix and exactly 3 fractional digits: `2026-08-01T09:14:22.481Z`. Not the framework default - configure the encoder.
serialisation.date: ISO 8601 date only, no time component: `2026-08-01`.
serialisation.money: `amount` and `total` and `daily_average` are decimal STRINGS in rupees with exactly two places. `*_paise` fields are integers. The client never divides by 100.
serialisation.nulls: An absent value is `null`, never omitted, never an empty string.

amount_grammar.note: Applied BEFORE Decimal(). CV-04 rules on written scale, which is necessary and not sufficient: Decimal('1.25e3') has scale 0 and would pass a scale-only check, and Decimal(' 12.50 ') parses where a strict pattern refuses. Rejects scientific notation, surrounding whitespace, a leading '+', and a bare '.50'.

serialisation.extra_fields: `extra="ignore"` model-wide. An unknown key is discarded, never 422 - `extra="forbid"` would reject the forged `user_id` of NEG-X-10, which must return 201 (SW-ADR-130).

request_models.note: `models` held only the RESPONSE shapes. `ExpenseCreate` and `Principal` appeared as bare strings in the route table and were defined nowhere - so the half of the contract every 422 test touches was outside the spec of record that SW-ADR-138 created precisely because hand-written shapes drift.
request_models.null_policy: An optional field may be sent as explicit `null` or omitted; the two are equivalent. Unknown keys are discarded, never rejected (`extra="ignore"`, CV-19 / SW-ADR-130).

fields.name: amount
fields.note: decimal string in rupees; a JSON number is 422 (amount.grammar)

fields.name: category_id
fields.note: ownership enforced by the composite FK, not a pre-read (SW-ADR-072)

fields.name: description
fields.note: empty or whitespace-only is normalised to null (SW-ADR-115)

ExpenseCreate.discarded_note: Discarded BEFORE validation, never 422 (SW-ADR-130). NEG-X-10 requires 201 for a forged user_id, so extra="forbid" is not available.

ExpenseUpdate.note: Every field optional; at least one must be present or 422 field.required with field='body'. The service sets updated_at (CV-09).

fields.name: currency
fields.note: the expenses service reads currency from HERE, never from the users table (CV-05, SRC-001 §3.4)

Principal.note: A response model, but listed here because the route table names it and `models` did not define it.
